commands.review_summary:
This PR filters non-finite numeric values and bounds OpenCode/OpenCode Go resetAt intervals before converting them to Int, with parser regression tests for oversized timestamps.

Reproducibility: yes. source-reproducible. Current main converts parsed OpenCode resetAt intervals directly to Int in both parser variants, so extreme malformed timestamps reach a known trap boundary without live credentials.

target.title: Prevent OpenCode reset timestamp overflow
target.body:
## Summary

- reject non-finite numeric values at the OpenCode and OpenCode Go parser boundary
- bound computed reset intervals before the trapping `Double`-to-`Int` conversion
- preserve valid usage windows while treating malformed reset timestamps as having no reset
- cover both infinite (`"1e309"`) and large finite (`"1e308"`) server values in both provider variants

## After-fix behavior proof

I ran the freshly built production parsers with the exact malformed server values through the focused executable test bundle. Both OpenCode variants now return the valid usage percentages and `resetInSec == 0` instead of terminating:

```text
OpenCodeUsageParserTests
  "ignores reset timestamps outside integer range"
  resetAt → "1e309" passed
  resetAt → "1e308" passed
  14 tests passed

OpenCodeGoUsageParserTests
  "ignores reset timestamps outside integer range"
  resetAt → "1e309" passed
  resetAt → "1e308" passed
  28 tests passed
```

The production path now checks the computed `Date.timeIntervalSince(now)` for finiteness and requires it to be strictly below `Double(Int.max)` before calling `Int(interval)`. Past timestamps still preserve the existing `0` behavior.

A live account/provider probe is intentionally not used here: repository policy says parser behavior should use focused fixtures and explicitly prohibits live provider/browser-cookie probes unless requested. These fixtures exercise the crash boundary directly without reading cookies or Keychain data.

## Testing

- `swift test --disable-sandbox --filter OpenCodeUsageParserTests`
- `swift test --disable-sandbox --filter OpenCodeGoUsageParserTests`
- `make check` (0 formatting or lint violations)
- `make test` (unrelated existing environment failure in `KeychainNoUIQueryTests`: `LAContext.interactionNotAllowed` remains false; focused suites pass)


## Production-path fixture proof

A temporary standalone executable linked against `CodexBarCore` called the public OpenCode and OpenCode Go fetchers with in-memory HTTP fixtures. This is outside Swift Testing and does not read live cookies or credentials. The temporary target was removed after the run.

```text
$ swift run --disable-sandbox --scratch-path .build OpenCodeProof
Build of product OpenCodeProof complete!
provider=OpenCode resetAt=1e309 rollingResetInSec=0 weeklyResetInSec=7200
provider=OpenCode resetAt=1e308 rollingResetInSec=0 weeklyResetInSec=7200
provider=OpenCodeGo resetAt=1e308 rollingResetInSec=0 weeklyResetInSec=7200
```

The malformed rolling reset is discarded without trapping, while the valid weekly reset remains intact.
